subject.title: Discord compaction still fails with provider_error_4xx after #90496 closure on 2026.6.5

question: For Discord sessions whose Codex native compaction fails with HTTP 403/provider_error_4xx, should OpenClaw keep failing closed with clearer guidance, rotate/preserve into a fresh usable session, or defer entirely to the timeout-partial-progress work?
rationale: Current source and docs prove the failure boundary, but the desired behavior changes session-state and provider-failure policy; automation should not choose whether to rotate, preserve, or fail closed for users.

options.title: Define Provider-4xx Recovery Policy
options.body: Keep this issue open and ask the agent/Codex owners to specify and prove the supported Discord recovery behavior for Codex 403 compaction failures.

options.title: Treat As Timeout-Adjacent Only
options.body: Close or merge into the timeout partial-progress work only if maintainers decide provider_error_4xx needs no separate recovery behavior beyond the existing compaction timeout fix.

options.title: Require Fresh Live Repro First
options.body: Pause implementation until a maintainer or reporter reproduces the current-main Discord/Codex 403 path and captures redacted logs or transcript proof.

recommendation.title: Define Provider-4xx Recovery Policy
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and ask the agent/Codex owners to specify and prove the supported Discord recovery behavior for Codex 403 compaction failures.

likelyOwner.reason: He has recent adjacent Codex app-server/harness ownership history and is the best available routing owner for a cross-boundary session/provider policy choice.
